item.title: 2026 World NEV Congress to spotlight global cooperation in Haikou
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
2026 World NEV Congress to spotlight global cooperation in Haikou HAIKOU, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 World New Energy Vehicle Congress (WNEVC) will take place from Sept. 22 to 24 in Haikou, capital of south China's Hainan Province, according to organizers on Wednesday. The event will be the eighth consecutive edition held in Hainan and the first since the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP) began island-wide special customs operations. Under the theme "Transformation & Upgrading, Resilient Growth," the congress is expected to attract delegates from more than 20 countries and regions, including executives from multinational automakers, representatives of international industry organizations and leading researchers. Discussions will cover technological innovation, industrial and supply chain resilience, low-carbon development and global cooperation in the new energy vehicle (NEV) sector. A key forum on globalization and the Hainan FTP will explore special-purpose vehicle manufacturing, intelligent connected vehicles, and opportunities arising from FTP policies. China's NEV exports continue to rise. In the first seven months of 2026, China exported 2.91 million NEVs, up 120 percent year on year, accounting for 47.4 percent of the country's total vehicle exports, industry data showed. In 2025, China sold 16.49 million NEVs, up 28.2 percent from a year earlier, representing 47.9 percent of all new vehicle sales. Against this backdrop, this year's congress will place a strong emphasis on international cooperation. It will again host a Sino-German forum on NEV cooperation and development, and for the first time, add a roundtable for Chinese and German auto parts companies. The World New Energy Vehicle Development Organization, established last September during the 2025 WNEVC, will participate in organizing the congress for the first time. Alongside the main forum, Hainan will host three thematic forums focusing on expert advice, intelligent connected and special-purpose vehicles, and the development of NEVs in cities. The congress will also see the launch of several industry platforms and the signing of projects involving vehicle manufacturing, export vehicle testing and intelligent connected vehicles. Launched in Hainan in 2019, the WNEVC has since held overseas sessions in Munich, California, Abu Dhabi, and Bangkok. Hainan aims to position itself as a manufacturing and overseas service hub for intelligent connected NEVs. From January to August this year, NEVs accounted for 66.14 percent of newly registered vehicles in Hainan. The province had 596,300 NEVs, making up 25.74 percent of its total vehicle fleet. item.title: China buffers global oil with strategic foresight
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
China buffers global oil with strategic foresight A recent international‑energy‑analysis video titled "China quietly saved the world," released by Max Fisher, a former columnist for The New York Times, has grabbed overseas public attention. The video spotlights a counter-intuitive phenomenon following the impact of the Iran war on global oil markets: Amid prevailing market fears of supply shortages and a global scramble among nations for alternative oil sources, China has substantially cut its crude oil imports and oil consumption, creating an unexpected buffer for the global oil market. According to Fisher, this shift stands as one major reason why global oil prices have not spiraled out of control as initially anticipated. As a strategic chokepoint for global energy transportation, the Strait of Hormuz has recently seen persistently tense navigation conditions, driving up the risk premium on international crude oil. According to historical market logic, when geopolitical conflicts trigger supply concerns, major consumer nations typically rush to procure and stockpile oil, while the widening supply-demand gap further drives up oil prices, which in turn feed into global inflation through energy costs. Following the recent escalation of tensions in the Middle East, market concerns have intensified that a rebound in energy prices could derail the global economic recovery, and expectations of an "oil scramble" briefly permeated the commodities trading markets. However, the Chinese market has offered a different response. Domestic refining and petrochemical companies have adjusted their production schedules in line with market conditions, flexibly and orderly slowing down new purchases of high-priced crude oil, thereby moderating the growth rate of imports from the demand side. With remarkable restraint, China has acted as a buffer for tight global supply demand balances. An article in The Wall Street Journal noted that China is propping up the world economy by importing a lot less oil; France's Le Figaro stated that China was helping "save" the world economy for a 2nd time since the 2008 financial crisis. For a long time, the global response to oil crises has primarily focused on the supply side, with major consumer nations largely forced to passively endure price fluctuations. However, this recent experience demonstrates that a massive consumer market can also serve as a buffer through production adjustments and inventory management, becoming a vital force in maintaining market equilibrium. Reuters noted that the dramatic reduction in China's seaborne crude oil imports since the start of the conflict means it is shouldering the bulk of the adjustment of lower volumes from the Middle East. The Financial Times also commented that the country's declining oil imports had emerged as a "critical variable reshaping global oil market dynamics." Why has China been able to buck the trend and chart a different trajectory? The confidence comes from China's strategic foresight. In previous years, when international oil prices stayed low, China steadily advanced the development of its commercial crude inventory system, gradually building up substantial reserves. During the current round of oil price increases, the country's domestic market has paused its routine pace of adding to commercial inventories, instead using previously built-up reserves to substitute for some high-priced imports. This approach has not only ensured the basic operating needs of China's domestic refining and petrochemical industries but has also avoided scrambling for supplies at high prices in the international market, which would have further exacerbated supply-demand tensions. "Grain in hand, no panic in heart" - this robust stockpile is the direct underpinning of China's flexibility in adjusting its import pace. After years of sustained efforts, China has established a smooth and efficient commercial inventory turnover system, while continuing to diversify its sources of crude oil imports to countries and regions such as Brazil and Africa, reducing its reliance on any single shipping route. More importantly, market-oriented refining and petrochemical operations have become increasingly mature, enabling companies to respond swiftly to price and risk signals and adjust their procurement and production plans accordingly. This diversified and flexible energy supply system gives China greater room to maneuver when faced with geopolitical disruptions. From a longer-term perspective, what is truly reshaping the logic of energy markets is a green transition that is steadily gaining depth and momentum. According to the International Energy Agency, electric vehicles alone displaced 1.5 million barrels a day of China's oil demand in the second quarter of 2026, far exceeding the market's previous expectations. China's rapid development of new energy is not only reshaping its own energy landscape, but also quietly changing the underlying dynamics of the global energy market. From once being a passive taker of fluctuations in international energy prices to becoming a proactive stabilizing force in the balance of the global market, the change reflects a consistent and steady logic underpinning China's energy development: keeping its own energy supply firmly in hand and using the certainty of its own development to navigate an uncertain external environment. In itself, this is one of the most tangible and enduring contributions China has made to global market stability. The author is a reporter with the People's Daily. item.title: China, CEE countries unveil 2030 vision for innovation cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
China, CEE countries unveil 2030 vision for innovation cooperation NINGBO, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China and Central and Eastern European countries (CEEC) unveiled a vision for innovation cooperation through 2030 on Wednesday, alongside a report reviewing a decade of collaboration in the field. The announcements were made at the 2026 China-CEEC Conference on Innovation Cooperation, which opened in Ningbo, east China's Zhejiang Province. The three-day event is co-hosted by China's Ministry of Science and Technology and Slovakia's Ministry of Economy. Around 450 government officials, diplomats, researchers, academics, entrepreneurs and young science and technology professionals from China and CEEC are attending the conference, which runs in both Ningbo and Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, under the theme "A Decade of Innovation, Building the Future Together." The conference features a ministerial meeting on science and technology innovation, as well as forums on artificial intelligence and robotics, biotechnology and green energy. At the opening ceremony, organizers released a 10-year report on China-CEEC innovation cooperation and a 2026 index measuring open innovation cooperation between Chinese cities and CEEC. Eleven agreements on industry-university-research collaboration and joint development of innovation platforms were signed, and the second China-CEEC Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competition was launched. At a ministerial meeting later Wednesday, senior representatives discussed cooperation opportunities in key fields and proposed the China-CEEC innovation cooperation 2030 vision. Representatives from countries including Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia and Slovenia attended the conference. Experts called for stronger cooperation among young researchers, more joint laboratories and concrete channels for collaborative research. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the conference. Since its launch in 2016, the event has been held five times in China, Slovakia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Serbia, promoting policy dialogue, joint research, personnel exchanges and technology cooperation. item.title: China firmly opposes U.S. groundless allegations on Chinese AI firms: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
China firmly opposes U.S. groundless allegations on Chinese AI firms: commerce ministry BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Commerce on Wednesday voiced firm opposition to the recent U.S. announcements that Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) companies are engaged in so-called industrial-scale efforts to distill capabilities from U.S. AI models, calling the accusations groundless and without legal basis. The U.S. move politicizes distillation, which is a normal technical and commercial issue in the AI industry, a ministry spokesperson said, adding the U.S. announcements are another proof of the country's pursuit of technological hegemony and computing power monopoly in the AI field, as well as its suppression of competition. Distillation is a common practice for mutual learning among AI models, which is essentially a neutral technical means used by global model companies including U.S. firms. It can help models enhance their learning efficiency, achieve more efficient utilization of human knowledge, and is significant for the development of the AI industry in various countries. China's open-source models are open to global enterprises, including those from the United States. Some U.S. enterprises have disclosed the distillation of a large number of Chinese models, the spokesperson said. However, the U.S. side has repeatedly and unilaterally accused Chinese enterprises of engaging in "industrial-scale" distillation, and smeared common practices as aggressive acts. This reflects the anxiety and double standards of the United States, the spokesperson said. The United States frequently threatened sanctions on and suppression of Chinese companies' distillation practices this year, aiming to maintain the U.S. monopoly in computing power and data, and prevent other countries from participating in the inclusive sharing of AI innovation achievements, the spokesperson said. China and the United States should handle the challenges and risks in the AI field in a proactive and responsible manner. The two heads of state have agreed to hold an inter-governmental dialogue on AI. China is willing to engage in constructive and professional discussions with the United States based on the principles of equality, mutual benefit and win-win cooperation, said the spokesperson. If the U.S. side takes actions to suppress Chinese AI enterprises under the pretext of targeting distillation, China will surely take resolute countermeasures, the spokesperson added. item.title: Xi's Central Asia, Middle East tour injects certainty, positive energy into world in flux
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Xi's Central Asia, Middle East tour injects certainty, positive energy into world in flux Chinese President Xi Jinping attends a group photo session during a welcome banquet held by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov ahead of the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus" meeting in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Sept. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye) BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping made a five-day trip to Central Asia and the Middle East from Aug. 30 to Sept. 3, during which he attended the 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit and paid state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt, sending strong messages that inject certainty and positive energy into a turbulent and changing world. The trip, observers say, was in step with the broader trends of the times as the Chinese president, with the shared future of humanity in mind, advanced a series of proposals on reforming and improving global governance. VISION FOR AN "EQUAL AND ORDERLY MULTIPOLAR WORLD" At the expanded SCO Plus Meeting in Bishkek, capital of Kyrgyzstan, Xi called for an "equal and orderly multipolar world" and a more just and equitable global governance system, with a stronger role for the United Nations. The SCO, since its establishment in 2001, has grown from a six-member Eurasian organization to a 27-nation family across Asia, Europe and Africa. In his speech, Xi said that sovereign equality and mutual respect are fundamental principles; balance, order and the rule of law are inherent requirements; multilateralism, dialogue and consultation are essential pathways; and mutual benefit, win-win, and inclusiveness are the way forward for development. These principles are rooted in Xi's vision for global governance, first articulated with the launch of the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) at last year's SCO Summit in China's coastal city of Tianjin, as the United Nations marked its 80th anniversary. The initiative has received support from nearly 160 countries and international organizations. The Group of Friends of Global Governance has been established in New York, Geneva and Vienna. The World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, the world's first intergovernmental international organization on AI, has been launched in Shanghai for AI governance. These efforts help turn the GGI into concrete actions. Put forward by Xi, the Global Governance Initiative, along with the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, and the Global Civilization Initiative, has been widely acclaimed, said SCO Secretary-General Nurlan Yermekbayev. "This is a complementary system of ideas and practical approaches aimed at addressing pressing contemporary challenges and building a just, peaceful, and sustainable world order," he said. During this trip, the Chinese president sought to promote peace, development and prosperity in both international and regional arenas. At SCO meetings, Xi outlined four proposals for advancing the organization's high-quality development and three suggestions for enhancing its role. During his state visit to Kyrgyzstan, Xi signed a bilateral treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation with his Kyrgyz counterpart. In Egypt, Xi proposed a four-point approach to building a new Middle East security architecture. DEVELOPMENT FOR THE PEOPLE In his talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov, Xi called for efforts to advance the building of a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future and better benefit the people of both countries. He urged high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, a flagship Belt and Road project linking China with Central Asia. Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and his wife Aigul Japarova in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) Addressing the SCO summit, Xi called on the SCO to put development first and open up the prospects for shared prosperity. The SCO, Xi said, should champion a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, consolidate cooperation in traditional areas such as trade and investment, connectivity, energy and resources, and expand cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, digital economy, green industry and green mining. The same emphasis on development and people's wellbeing was evident during Xi's visit to Egypt. In a joint communique, China praised Egypt's Decent Life Initiative for its efforts to improve people's living standards, while Egypt expressed appreciation for the Global Development Initiative. As Xi once put it, "People's sense of gain should be the goal of domestic governance and global governance, and we should continue to provide confidence and stable expectations for the people." MUTUAL LEARNING In a signed article published ahead of his visit to Kyrgyzstan, Xi wrote about the ancient Silk Road as a witness to the long-standing friendship between the two peoples, citing the stories of historical figures such as diplomat Zhang Qian, monk Xuanzang and poet Li Bai, whose legacy is seen as promoting civilizational exchanges between China and Kyrgyzstan. During his visit to Egypt, Xi, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, visited the Grand Egyptian Museum, where the legacy of ancient Egypt unfolds against the backdrop of the millennia-old pyramids. Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi, tour the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) Xi and Sisi, together with their spouses, spent more than one hour touring the museum, home to more than 100,000 precious artifacts. They toured the grand galleries, posing for a photo before a towering statue of Ramses II, one of the most famous pharaohs of Egypt, as curators delivered a swift primer on pharaonic history. "This museum is a book with endless pages," Xi said. The museum visit also underscored Xi's longstanding emphasis on exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations. Over the years, Xi's overseas trips have taken him to museums and historic sites, from the Amir Timur Museum in Uzbekistan to the ancient Maya ruins of Chichen Itza in Mexico. At home, he also invited foreign leaders to visit China's historic sites, ranging from the Forbidden City to the ancient irrigation system Dujiangyan and the over 600-year-old Temple of Heaven. At the Grand Egyptian Museum, Xi called on the two countries to promote inclusive coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, and pool greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. The remarks echoed Xi's message to Sisi on the museum's opening last year, in which Xi highlighted the vibrant cultural and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, citing the successful exhibition on ancient Egyptian civilization in Shanghai and joint archaeological exploration into the pyramids at Saqqara, located south of Cairo. "It is encouraging to see the two ancient civilizations reaching out to each other, with the two peoples growing ever closer through mutual understanding and affinity," Xi said. item.title: Hong Kong, Macao students interact with Shenzhou-23 crew from orbit during "Tiangong Class"
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Hong Kong, Macao students interact with Shenzhou-23 crew from orbit during "Tiangong Class" John Lee, chief executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), and students pose for photos during a live space lecture of the "Tiangong Class" Hong Kong and Macao Designated Session in Hong Kong, south China, Sept. 9, 2026. (Photo by Lui Sui Wai/Xinhua) HONG KONG, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The "Tiangong Class" Hong Kong and Macao Designated Session was held simultaneously in Hong Kong and Macao on Wednesday morning, as the three Chinese astronauts of the Shenzhou-23 crew currently carrying out a manned space mission at the Tiangong space station delivered a live space lecture for students. Shenzhou-23 mission commander Zhu Yangzhu, astronaut Zhang Zhiyuan and Hong Kong's first payload specialist Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, delivered an engaging and vivid science lesson to the young people of Hong Kong and Macao. The event was jointly organized by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) government, the Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) government and the China Manned Space Agency, with the main classroom set up at Lai's alma mater, Tsuen Wan Public Ho Chuen Yiu Memorial College in Hong Kong. A total of 160 Hong Kong students and 50 Macao students attended the main venue in person, joined by school principals, teachers, youth representatives, and tech professionals from both cities. The HKSAR government and the Macao SAR government also arranged for teachers and students of primary and secondary schools to watch the live broadcast simultaneously on campus. During the session, the three astronauts demonstrated scientific experiments in the unique space environment in real time and shared glimpses of daily life aboard the space station. They conducted a series of science demonstrations, including baking a cake in the space kitchen, wringing out a wet towel, and tending the space vegetable garden. Lai also showcased the operating procedures for MUSICO, a lightweight, high-resolution, high-precision carbon dioxide and methane point-source detector developed under the leadership of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. Throughout the lecture, the astronauts answered questions from students on space science and astronaut life in orbit. John Lee, HKSAR's chief executive, asked Lai whether she had received the letters sent by the students. In response, Lai said she had read through every letter from home, pledging to honor their trust and spare no effort to complete her in-orbit mission. She added that her spaceflight reflected the country's strong support for Hong Kong. Kong Chi Meng, director of the Education and Youth Development Bureau of the Macao SAR government, said that the lecture was not only a vivid lesson in science and technology education, but also a profound lesson in patriotism, with the three astronauts serving as exemplary role models for students. item.title: Polished lacquerware well inherited in N China's Shanxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Polished lacquerware well inherited in N China's Shanxi Upon stepping into the China Polished Lacquerware Museum in the ancient city of Pingyao, north China's Shanxi Province, one will find artisans at their workbenches, gently sweeping brushes across lacquerware bases as gold powder slowly settles into the patterns. Photo shows Pingyao polished lacquerware. (People's Daily Online/Wang Fan) As a national-level intangible cultural heritage, Pingyao polished lacquerware craft involves six specialized trades and 66 intricate processes. "Gold painting and polychrome decoration are at the very heart of Pingyao polished lacquerware," said Lei Tianyong, an arts and crafts master. Lei Tianyong carefully examines the details of the gold painting and polychrome decoration process. (People's Daily Online/Wang Fan) An artisan uses a whetstone to polish and refine a lacquerware base. (People's Daily Online/Wang Fan) The lacquer-making process is painstaking and demanding. For years, Lei has pondered how to inspire young people to devote themselves to learning the craft. In 2009, he began exploring ways to bring the intangible cultural heritage into schools, and in 2011, he officially began enrolling and teaching students. "We take in around 30 students each year. Many are initially drawn by curiosity, but those who stay must be able to endure the solitude," Lei said. "Purely handmade works cannot be replaced by AI. They embody decades of accumulated skill. You must have patience when practicing a craft. First, you have to settle down, preserve the traditional foundations, and only then talk about innovation," he added. Chen Haiming, an arts and crafts master, works on a piece of polished lacquerware. (People's Daily Online/Wang Fan) Inside the exhibition hall of the China Polished Lacquerware Museum, lacquerware pieces stand quietly on display. The museum's centerpiece, depicting cats frolicking in spring, was painted over three years by Xue Shengjin, an arts and crafts master and a national-level representative inheritor of intangible cultural heritage. Nearby is a polished lacquerware piece by arts and crafts master Chen Haiming, depicting 128 immortals in flowing robes, with mineral pigments that remain vivid to this day. A young artisan applies gold painting and polychrome decoration to a Pingyao polished lacquerware base. (People's Daily Online/Wang Fan) In the museum's educational workshop, young people gather around workbenches to watch artisans demonstrate fabric wrapping, ash application and polishing, and to feel the texture of natural lacquer for themselves. The workshop is now a study and practice base for primary and secondary school students in Shanxi, allowing them to see, hear and experience intangible cultural heritage up close. Visitors select Pingyao polished lacquerware jewelry boxes. (People's Daily Online/Wang Fan) Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Global Services, Shared Prosperity: 2026 CIFTIS opened in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Global Services, Shared Prosperity: 2026 CIFTIS opened in Beijing People visit the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) at Shougang Park in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 9, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Han) BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) opened Wednesday in Beijing, as China steps up efforts to expand opening-up in services trade at the outset of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Running through Sept. 13 at Shougang Park, a former industrial site and venue for the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics, the fair has drawn participants from 90 countries, regions and international organizations, with over 1,800 companies exhibiting on-site. Themed "Global Services, Shared Prosperity," this year's CIFTIS features a Global Trade in Services Summit, co-hosted for the first time by the World Intellectual Property Organization. A series of forums and business matchmaking activities will also be held during the fair. The core exhibition area also debuts a showcase of more than 140 innovation cases spanning all 12 categories of services trade, including artificial intelligence, large language models, and intelligent agents, offering a glimpse of where China's services sector is headed. item.title: Xi extends Teachers' Day greetings, urges nurturing capable youth for national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Xi extends Teachers' Day greetings, urges nurturing capable youth for national rejuvenation BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has extended greetings to teachers and educators across the country ahead of Teachers' Day, which is celebrated annually on Sept. 10. In a congratulatory message, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called on teachers nationwide to enhance their professional competence and capabilities, and foster a new generation of young people to shoulder the mission of realizing national rejuvenation. Over long periods of time, teachers across the country have devoted themselves to education, imparting knowledge and nurturing young minds, said Xi, commending their significant contributions to the cause of the Party and the state. Xi emphasized the importance of carrying out the basic task of fostering virtue through education and cultivating a high standard of professional integrity and conduct on the new journey. He also called for fostering public respect for educators, encouraging support for education, and bringing together all efforts to make China a leading country in education. China boasts the largest education system in the world, having roughly 440,000 schools at all levels and of all types, with 280 million students and 18.7 million teachers.
